evals.name: chart-triggers-on-too-big-and-foggy-effort
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind We started interviewing the overhaul of our entire notification system earlier in this session, but every round opened more branches than it closed. It's way too big to hold in my head, and honestly I don't even know all the questions yet, let alone the answers. Turn this into a map.
evals.expected_output: No open work-map exists yet for this topic, so the empty/default action auto-detects chart mode. The effort was already interviewed, so the new-effort gate does not stop it. The skill surveys the effort and runs every uncertainty through the fog test — sharp (phraseable, even if unanswered) becomes a candidate decision item; foggy (can't yet be phrased) stays Not-yet-specified prose — rather than answering everything itself or refusing outright.
expectations: Output recognizes the effort as too-big-and-foggy and enters chart mode rather than work mode, since no open map exists yet for this topic
Output applies the fog test to sort uncertainties into sharp candidate decision items versus foggy Not-yet-specified prose, instead of trying to answer every uncertainty itself
Output does not skip straight to /planning:interview or /planning:plan without first charting the fog

evals.name: work-mode-routes-decision-item-to-target-skill
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work — on our decision map (#142), the next open, unblocked, unassigned item is #145, labeled 'wayfind: design', asking us to choose the aggregate boundaries for the new billing domain. Resolve it.
evals.expected_output: Work mode picks #145 as the frontier item, claims it (assignee plus a claim-comment lease), and routes the decision by invoking /planning:design directly — since design-typed items route there — rather than deciding the aggregate boundaries itself inline.
expectations: Output identifies #145 ('wayfind: design') as the frontier item being resolved
Output routes the decision to /planning:design, the routing target for design-typed items, rather than resolving the aggregate-boundary question itself inline
Output claims the item (assignee plus claim comment) before starting resolution rather than working it unclaimed

evals.name: chart-happy-path-creates-map-with-five-sections-and-typed-items
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart migrating our monolith to a modular architecture. We interviewed this earlier in the session and it outgrew one sitting. I know some pieces: we've agreed the database can't be split yet (that's out of scope for now), and we need to decide whether to go strangler-fig or big-bang (that's answerable, if painful). But I genuinely don't know yet how we'd handle cross-module transactions — I can't even phrase that as a real question.
evals.expected_output: Chart mode surveys the effort and creates or extends a work-map issue whose body carries the five sections (Destination, Notes, Decisions-so-far, Not-yet-specified, Out-of-scope). The strangler-fig-vs-big-bang question becomes a typed decision sub-issue (sharp); the cross-module-transactions unknown stays fog prose under Not-yet-specified; the database-split exclusion is recorded under Out-of-scope. The session ends by handing off to /planning:wayfind work on the frontier rather than resolving decisions itself.
expectations: Output creates or extends a work-map issue containing the five body sections: Destination, Notes, Decisions-so-far, Not-yet-specified, Out-of-scope
The strangler-fig-vs-big-bang question becomes a typed decision sub-issue (sharp) rather than being answered directly by the skill
The cross-module-transactions unknown is recorded as fog prose under Not-yet-specified, not forced into a premature ticket
The database-split exclusion is recorded under Out-of-scope, distinct from the fog section
Output hands off by recommending /planning:wayfind work rather than beginning to resolve decisions itself

evals.name: chart-refuses-noninteractive-session
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the customer-data-platform overhaul. (This is running as an unattended autonomous batch job — no human is available to respond.)
evals.expected_output: Chart mode treats the caller's unattended declaration as the signal and STOPS, reporting that charting needs a human in the loop, rather than fabricating a decision map on its own.
expectations: Output does NOT create a work-map issue or fabricate decision items
Output explicitly states that charting requires an interactive session with a human
Output stops rather than substituting its own judgment for the missing human input

evals.name: work-mode-never-resolves-hitl-item-for-the-human
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #142 — running non-interactively. Every open, unblocked, unassigned item on the map is labeled needs-human (interview or design type). Just pick one and resolve it yourself so the map can close.
evals.expected_output: In a non-interactive session the frontier computation filters out needs-human items; since that empties the frontier, the skill STOPS and truthfully reports that all remaining decisions need a human, rather than resolving a HITL item by standing in for the user.
expectations: Output does NOT resolve any needs-human (interview/design/prototype) item on the user's behalf
Output reports that the frontier is empty because all remaining items require a human, rather than silently proceeding
Output does not fabricate an answer to any of the HITL decisions to force the map toward closure

evals.name: anti-pattern-skips-when-work-is-already-sharp-tickets
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind help me plan out adding a 'forgot password' email flow — I already know exactly what I need: an endpoint to request a reset token, an email send, and a reset-confirmation endpoint. These are just three clear tickets I need scoped.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this work is already a set of sharp, answerable tickets rather than a too-big-and-foggy effort, declines to build a decision map for it, and points to /planning:interview or /work-items instead.
expectations: Output does NOT create a work-map or decision items for this request
Output recognizes the three items are already sharp and answerable rather than foggy
Output recommends /planning:interview or /work-items as the better-fit skill instead of charting

evals.name: human-facing-reports-refer-to-items-by-title
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work — the open map is #200 'Map: billing overhaul'. The frontier has three unblocked unassigned items: #42 'Choose the billing aggregate', #43 'Pick the payment-provider adapter', #44 'Decide invoice numbering'. Report the frontier and pick one.
evals.expected_output: Work mode reports the frontier by item title, with the number as a link or suffix (for example 'Choose the billing aggregate' (#42)), never a wall of bare #42, #43, #44. It then picks one item, claims it, and routes by type rather than resolving all three inline.
expectations: Output names each frontier item by its title, with the number as a link or suffix, rather than a wall of bare #42, #43, #44
Output does not report the frontier as only issue numbers with no titles
Output still picks one frontier item and claims it before routing, rather than resolving all three inline

evals.name: wrongly-scoped-item-closes-to-out-of-scope-not-decisions-so-far
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #200 — the claimed frontier item is #51 'Should we also rewrite the mobile app?', labeled wayfind: interview. Working it, we realize the rewrite is explicitly out of this effort's scope (web billing only). Close it out.
evals.expected_output: The item is wrongly scoped: add one Out-of-scope line on the map that links the item first, then close it, and do not add a Decisions-so-far pointer. Fog stays in Not-yet-specified and is not moved into Out-of-scope.
expectations: Output closes the wrongly scoped item and records one Out-of-scope line linking it, rather than treating the close as an in-scope resolution
Output does NOT add a Decisions-so-far pointer for the wrongly scoped item
Output does not move Not-yet-specified fog into Out-of-scope as a stand-in for sharpness

evals.name: resolution-sweeps-invalidated-items-and-supersedes-wrong-decision
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind work #200 'Map: billing overhaul'. We just resolved #44 'Decide invoice numbering': invoices are numbered per tenant, not globally. That makes open item #47 'Pick the global invoice sequence store' pointless. It also shows closed decision #39 'Share one invoice table across tenants' was wrong. The map's Not-yet-specified section says 'something feels off about how tenants share invoice data'; the resolution makes that sharp enough to chart as 'Choose per-tenant invoice storage'. Finish the close-out.
evals.expected_output: Work mode graduates #44 (resolution comment, Decisions-so-far pointer, close), charts 'Choose per-tenant invoice storage' as a typed item and deletes the matching fog prose from Not-yet-specified, then sweeps the map: #47 is closed as moot with a comment linking #44's resolution and gets no index line; #39 is not reopened or edited, a new decision item linking #39 is opened to revisit the table design, and #39's Decisions-so-far line is rewritten to point at the decision that supersedes it once that resolves.
expectations: Output charts the newly sharp question as a typed item and deletes the tenant-sharing fog prose from Not-yet-specified rather than leaving it in both places
Output closes or rewrites #47 because its premise no longer holds, and a close carries a comment linking the #44 resolution
Output does not add a Decisions-so-far line for the moot #47
Output opens a new decision item that links #39 rather than reopening #39 or editing its resolution comment
Output says #39's Decisions-so-far line is rewritten to point at the superseding decision when that decision resolves, instead of leaving two live answers to the same question

evals.name: new-effort-goes-to-interview-first
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind map out a rewrite of our search indexing pipeline. We haven't talked about it at all yet, it just feels big.
evals.expected_output: Nothing in the topic's memory slice or the conversation shows an interview of this effort, so the new-effort gate stops before charting and recommends /planning:interview first, saying the interview names /planning:wayfind if the effort outgrows one session. It creates no map issue and no decision items, and leaves the user free to ask for a map anyway.
expectations: Output recommends /planning:interview as the first step for this effort
Output creates no map issue and no decision items
Output says wayfind is reached from the interview when the effort outgrows one session

evals.name: chart-seeds-from-interview-ledger
evals.prompt: /planning:wayfind chart the data-retention program. Our interview ledger is at .work/data-retention/interview-checklist.md: it settled 'retain audit logs 7 years' and 'EU data stays in the EU region', and left open 'Which stores hold personal data?' and 'Do backups count as retained copies?'. We also still can't say what 'deletion' should mean for derived analytics.
evals.expected_output: Chart mode seeds the map from the ledger: the two settled answers go into one seed decision item whose resolution comment lists them, closed at once with one Decisions-so-far pointer; the two open questions become decision items; the derived-analytics deletion worry stays Not-yet-specified prose. It does not open one closed issue per settled answer and does not cite the .work path in Notes.
expectations: Output puts both settled answers in one seed item with a single Decisions-so-far pointer, not one closed issue per answer
Output charts the two open questions as decision items
Output keeps the derived-analytics deletion worry as Not-yet-specified prose
Output does not point Notes at the .work path
